title: Course quality
prompt: For each course_id, show quality, the average of grade divided by 100 rounded to 2 decimals, and low_pct, the percentage of its enrolments with a grade below 70, rounded to 2 decimals. Ignore enrolments with no grade.
hints: Filter NULL grades, then use a per-row ratio and a conditional count.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (15, 8, 5, 75, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT course_id, ROUND(AVG(grade / 100.0), 2) AS quality, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN grade < 70 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS low_pct FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL GROUP BY course_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT course_id, ROUND(AVG(grade / 100), 2) AS quality, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN grade < 70 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS low_pct FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL GROUP BY course_id;

SELECT course_id, ROUND(AVG(grade / 100.0), 2) AS quality, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN grade < 70 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100 / COUNT(*), 2) AS low_pct FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL GROUP BY course_id;

title: Monthly summary
prompt: For each month like 2024-01 and each status, show month, status, the number of orders as orders, and the number placed by customer 1 as customer_one.
hints: Group by two values, with a conditional count.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); UPDATE orders SET customer_id = 1 WHERE id = 11;

solutions: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, status, COUNT(*) AS orders, SUM(CASE WHEN customer_id = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS customer_one FROM orders GROUP BY month, status;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, status, COUNT(*) AS orders, COUNT(*) AS customer_one FROM orders GROUP BY month, status;
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, status, COUNT(*) AS orders, SUM(CASE WHEN customer_id = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS customer_one FROM orders GROUP BY month;

title: Different courses per student
prompt: A student can repeat a course. Show each student_id and how many different courses they've taken, as courses.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT student_id, COUNT(DISTINCT course_id) AS courses FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT student_id, COUNT(course_id) AS courses FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id;
SELECT student_id, COUNT(*) AS courses FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id;

title: Daily users
prompt: For the 7 days ending 2024-01-05 inclusive, show each date as day and how many different users had a session as users.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); UPDATE sessions SET session_date = '2024-01-05' WHERE id IN (11, 12); UPDATE sessions SET session_date = '2024-01-06' WHERE id = 13;

solutions: SELECT session_date AS day, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS users FROM sessions WHERE session_date BETWEEN '2023-12-30' AND '2024-01-05' GROUP BY session_date;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT session_date AS day, COUNT(*) AS users FROM sessions WHERE session_date BETWEEN '2023-12-30' AND '2024-01-05' GROUP BY session_date;
SELECT session_date AS day, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS users FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date;

title: Popular referrers
prompt: Show the referrer_id of users who have invited at least 2 people.
hints: Leave out users with no referrer, since NULL isn't a person.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); INSERT INTO users VALUES (10, 'vega', NULL, '2024-03-02'), (12, 'wren', NULL, '2024-03-03');

solutions: SELECT referrer_id FROM users WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY referrer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT referrer_id FROM users GROUP BY referrer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
wrongSolutions.why: NULL can appear as a group

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT referrer_id FROM users WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY referrer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2;

title: Invite counts
prompt: Show each referrer_id that isn't NULL, and how many users they invited as invited, sorted by referrer_id.
solutions: SELECT referrer_id, COUNT(*) AS invited FROM users WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY referrer_id ORDER BY referrer_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT referrer_id, COUNT(*) AS invited FROM users GROUP BY referrer_id ORDER BY referrer_id;
SELECT referrer_id, COUNT(*) AS invited FROM users WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY referrer_id ORDER BY invited;
